evals.prompt: Is branch feat/invoice-rounding ready to ship? Run the full pre-ship check. All gate outputs I collected are in the attached file. Give me the verdict.
evals.expected_output: Full mode: emits the gate matrix with tests FAIL and coverage FAIL (lint/type/build PASS), calls the email-queue test failure pre-existing with an explicit call that it blocks shipping, includes a Verdict line of NOT-READY, and applies no fixes.
assertions: The reply contains the full gate matrix (a table with one row per gate), not just a signal-only list.
The matrix shows tests as FAIL and coverage as FAIL (78.4% against the 80% threshold, tied to the untested new branches in round.ts).
The reply names the email-queue test failure as pre-existing or unrelated to this change.
The reply states explicitly whether that pre-existing failure blocks shipping (it is a required gate, so it does block or needs a decision).
The reply includes a line starting with 'Verdict:' whose value is NOT-READY, not READY-TO-SHIP or NEEDS-ATTENTION.
The reply does not claim to have edited code, fixed tests, or pushed anything, and only reports or recommends next steps.

evals.prompt: Just run the checks on this small change before I hand it off. Context (diff, CI state, scripts) is in the attached file.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the latest CI run on the same SHA is fully green and nothing changed since, so it logs 'already verified at 9d03a7f' and skips re-running. If it describes what it would run otherwise, it is the narrow order lint, types, targeted tests, not the full matrix.
assertions: The reply says the change is already verified at SHA 9d03a7f (or equivalent wording citing that SHA).
The reply skips or declines to re-run the checks because CI on the same commit is already fully green.
The reply notes that a re-run is only needed if code changes after that CI run.
The reply does not propose the full gate matrix (no coverage, sonar, sentry or schema-drift gates for this one-file change).
If the reply lists any checks to run anyway, they follow the order lint, then type check, then targeted tests.

evals.prompt: Read the attached run and the developer's message. Do what they ask and tell me how you respond.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to call this verified because a required security gate was skipped for convenience (not because it is not applicable). Verdict PARTIAL or NOT-READY, lists the skipped gate and why it is required, and will not merge without explicit acknowledgement from the user of what was skipped.
assertions: The reply does not claim the change is verified or ready to ship.
The reply gives a PARTIAL (or NOT-READY / NEEDS-ATTENTION) verdict rather than PASS.
The reply names the security scan (npm audit plus semgrep) as the skipped required gate.
The reply says the skip is not a valid 'not applicable' reason, because dependencies and auth code changed and the stated reason is only that it is slow.
The reply says it will not merge PR #77 unless the user explicitly acknowledges what was skipped.
The reply offers to run the security scan or asks the user for explicit acknowledgement as the way forward.

evals.prompt: Is branch feat/invoice-currency ready to ship? CI is green on this commit. Run the full pre-ship check with --strict. All gate outputs I collected are in the attached file. Give me the verdict.
evals.expected_output: Full mode does not short-circuit on the green CI run. CI is marked PASS for the SHA, but schema-drift (pending migration) and sentry (new error since the push) are still reported, and the verdict is NOT-READY or NEEDS-ATTENTION, never READY-TO-SHIP.
assertions: The reply does not stop with 'already verified' or skip the remaining gates because CI on the same SHA is green.
The reply may mark the CI gate PASS for c7d21fe, but still evaluates the other applicable gates.
The reply reports the schema-drift problem: the currency column change has no migration.
The reply reports the new Sentry error that appeared after the push (column Invoice.currency does not exist).
The reply includes a 'Verdict:' line that is NOT-READY or NEEDS-ATTENTION, not READY-TO-SHIP.
The reply does not claim to have created a migration or fixed anything, and only reports or recommends next steps.
